Phase 1 of the session (reading the roadmap, the register, checkpoint IV, Carl's 2026-11-05 rulings, the statistics kernel's names, the cosmology kernel's flrw.js, the 248 and 251 kernels and the sibling contracts for 245, 247, 248, 249, 251 and 252) preceded it and fixed nothing here from a result. The only numbers computed before this commit are closed forms and root-finds of closed forms (the truncation fixed point of the clipping rule, the half-number radius of a truncated r^-2 sphere, the inverse of the normal quartile at 3/4), none of them the output of the kernel.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured (a file not supplied, a tool not installed) is NOT RUN and says why, and nothing is fetched. No published redshift, velocity dispersion, virial mass, projection factor, gas mass, luminosity, solar absolute magnitude, biweight tuning constant, morphology fraction, catalogue value, cosmological parameter of a survey, licence term or citation detail is typed anywhere from memory. The validation cosmology below, every invented cluster, every tuning choice a leg passes in (the biweight constants 6 and 9, the projection factor of the toy worlds, the solar absolute magnitude, the neighbour count) and every bound are round numbers or closed forms chosen for the test and are claims about nothing; whether a tuning choice equals a conventional published one is not asserted. Every authentic fact would come from a file Carl supplied under tests/fixtures/clusters/authentic/ with its source, its terms as read from a saved copy and its retrieval date in that directory's SOURCES.json. Every synthetic world is labelled synthetic and carries its truth manifest. Failed legs are never rescued by moving a bound, re-reading a committed threshold after a result or counting a case out; the alternative is recorded as a question for Carl in GALAXY_CLUSTERS.md. An amendment is recorded in this file before any validator run it concerns, with its reason and the statement that no bound moved.

scope.built: the kernel js/kernels/galaxy/clusters/ (not re-exported by the galaxy index): rest-frame velocities from redshifts; cluster membership by an iterated sigma clip with its iterations stated; the velocity dispersion (the plain estimator with the clip's Gaussian truncation correction, or, as a caller option with a caller-supplied tuning, the biweight scale) with its uncertainty (analytic or a seeded bootstrap), the correction for stated per-galaxy velocity errors, and a Gaussianity and a contamination diagnostic; the projected geometry (great-circle separations, the angular-diameter distance of the caller's cosmology, the half-number radius and the harmonic radius); the virial mass M = K sigma^2 R / G with the projection factor K supplied by the caller with its uncertainty and source, and the interval that carries the dispersion term, the radius term and the factor's term separately; the cluster's light from the members' photometry and the mass-to-light ratio; the morphology-density relation as a measured fraction in bins of projected local density with exact binomial intervals; the baryon budget from a cited gas mass; labelled synthetic generators
scope.notBuilt: the cluster panel (the redshift histogram, membership, the dispersion, the mass with both uncertainty terms, the morphology-density plot), the investigations 'Zwicky's problem' and the upper depth of 'Where galaxies live', the model page section, the instructor materials, Spanish strings, every pack (the Coma pack's re-sourcing and the retirement of the 'illustrative' label of Prompt 123 included), the second cluster, any X-ray model, any non-Gaussian or substructure model, any background-subtracted dispersion, any luminosity-function correction for light below the limit: the consumers rule (Carl, 2026-11-05) holds the panel, the lessons and the packs until a gate passes, and Prompt 250's Run condition asks for a rights decision on the cluster table that was not made (nothing was fetched)
scope.authenticTierNotRun: E1 to E4 (Coma's published dispersion and virial mass under a fixed contract, the pinned independent analysis of the same table, the morphology-density relation on a classified table, the mass-to-light ratio): no table was supplied and nothing was fetched

analysisRule.R1: Units inside the kernel: kilometres per second for velocities (a caller who holds m/s divides by 1000), metres for the mass computation (the tree's parsec times 1e6 for the Mpc), radians for angles at the boundary of the great-circle function (the pipeline takes degrees for ra and dec and says so), kilograms for mass (the tree's SOLAR_MASS_KG for solar masses). The tree's G_SI and C_SI. There is no default cosmology, projection factor, solar absolute magnitude, biweight tuning constant, neighbour count or catalogue.
analysisRule.R2: The rest-frame velocity of a galaxy at redshift z in a cluster at redshift z_c is v = c (z - z_c) / (1 + z_c), c = 299792.458 km/s. The exact special-relativistic relative velocity of the same pair differs from this by a relative z_rel/2 + O(z_rel^3), with z_rel = (1 + z)/(1 + z_c) - 1; the contract keeps the linear form and prices the difference in leg A1. The cluster redshift is the mean of the members' redshifts (the biweight location for the biweight option), so the members' mean velocity is zero.
analysisRule.R3: Pre-selection, in this order: a galaxy is kept if its redshift is finite and positive, it lies within the caller's angular aperture (a physical radius in Mpc converted with the angular-diameter distance at the caller's redshift guess zGuess, then recomputed once at the first pass's cluster redshift, two passes in all), and, if the caller gives them, it lies inside the caller's redshift window and within velocityExtentKms of the median redshift. A table with a different selection is the caller's, and the kernel's statements are about the table it is given.
analysisRule.R4: Membership is an iterated sigma clip on u = c (z - z_0) / (1 + z_0), z_0 the median redshift of the pre-selected galaxies. Pass 0: centre = median(u), scale = 1.4826... MAD(u) (1.4826... is 1 / Phi^-1(3/4), computed from the statistics kernel's normal quantile, not typed). Each pass keeps the galaxies with |u - centre| <= kappa scale, then sets centre = mean(u of the kept), scale = their sample standard deviation (n - 1), and repeats. kappa = 3 and at most 10 passes. It stops when the kept set is the same as the previous pass's (converged). A set that has not converged after 10 passes, or that returns to an earlier set that is not its predecessor, is 'not-constrained' with code 'clip-not-converged'. kappa must exceed sqrt(3) (below it the truncated-Gaussian fixed point of R6 is 0), else 'refused' with code 'bad-clip-level'.
analysisRule.R5: A cluster needs at least 20 members after the clip (MIN_MEMBERS = 20): fewer is 'not-constrained' with code 'too-few-members'; the interval of a dispersion from 20 members is about 16 percent in sigma and the kernel says so. The aperture's pre-selection needs at least 20 galaxies as well, same code.
analysisRule.R6: Plain estimator: s = sqrt(sum (v - mean v)^2 / (n - 1)) over the members. The clip truncates a Gaussian parent at kappa s, which lowers the variance of the kept set; at the fixed point of R4 the kept set is the parent restricted to |v - mean| <= kappa s, so s^2 = sigma^2 V(kappa s / sigma) with V(a) = 1 - 2 a phi(a) / (2 Phi(a) - 1), phi and Phi the standard normal density and distribution. Writing x = s / sigma, the factor x*(kappa) is the root of x^2 = V(kappa x) in (0, 1]. The reported dispersion is sigma_hat = s / x*(kappa) (the correction is on by default and reported beside the raw s; the option truncationCorrection false returns s). The correction is exact for a Gaussian parent and says nothing for any other; the Gaussianity diagnostic of R9 is its guard.
analysisRule.R7: Per-galaxy velocity errors e_i, when the caller supplies zErr_i (redshift errors, converted with c / (1 + z_c)): the intrinsic variance is s^2 - mean(e_i^2) before the truncation correction; a non-positive result is 'not-constrained' with code 'errors-exceed-scatter'. Error of the intrinsic dispersion: d sigma_int = (s / sigma_int) d s. The correction is defined for the plain estimator only; with the biweight option a supplied zErr is refused with code 'errors-with-biweight'.
analysisRule.R8: Uncertainty of the dispersion. Analytic (default): sigma_s = sigma_hat / sqrt(2 (n - 1)), exact for the standard deviation of a Gaussian sample to the order stated (the truncation lowers the sampling variance by under 2 percent, which makes the interval slightly conservative). Bootstrap (option): seeded case bootstrap over the members with the statistics kernel (draws default 1000, percentile interval at the stated level), re-computing the estimator, not the clip. Neither prices the uncertainty of the membership (a galaxy near the edge of the clip or an interloper inside it); leg R4 prices the contamination.
analysisRule.R9: Diagnostics reported with every dispersion, and flags (a flag does not change a number, it blocks the claim): the excess kurtosis G2 of the members' velocities (the unbiased estimator) with its standard error under a Gaussian parent, SE = sqrt(24 n (n-1)^2 / ((n-3)(n-2)(n+3)(n+5))); the flag 'non-gaussian' when |G2| > 3 SE. The contamination estimate: the number of galaxies of the pre-selection outside the clip window, divided by the velocity width outside it within velocityExtentKms of the cluster, times the window's width, is the expected number of field galaxies inside the window; the flag 'contaminated' when that exceeds 0.10 of the members (needs velocityExtentKms; without it the diagnostic is 'unknown' and no flag is raised). The kernel applies no background correction to the dispersion.
analysisRule.R10: Geometry. The separation between two sky positions (degrees) is the great-circle angle by the haversine formula; the physical projected separation is that angle times the angular-diameter distance D_A(z_c) of the caller's flat cosmology (the cosmology kernel's flrw.js; H0 in km/s/Mpc, Om + OL = 1 required, else 'refused'). Half-number radius: the median of the members' projected distances from the caller's centre. Harmonic radius: N (N - 1) / 2 divided by the sum over member pairs of 1 / R_ij. Uncertainties by a seeded case bootstrap (draws default 1000; the pairs of one resampled galaxy with itself are skipped); the centre is the caller's and its own uncertainty is not carried. A radius is a property of the aperture the members were selected in (R3), not of the cluster alone; the mass is the mass within that aperture under the stated factor.
analysisRule.R11: Virial mass M = K sigma^2 R / G, sigma in m/s, R in metres, G the tree's. The factor K is supplied as {value, sigma, source, radiusKind} (radiusKind 'half-number' or 'harmonic', which must be the radius the caller chose); a missing value, a non-positive value or sigma, an empty source or a radiusKind that does not match is refused (codes 'missing-factor', 'bad-factor', 'missing-factor-source', 'factor-radius-mismatch'). ln M = ln K + 2 ln sigma + ln R - ln G, so to first order the standard deviation of ln M is sqrt((sigma_K/K)^2 + (2 sigma_sigma/sigma)^2 + (sigma_R/R)^2) (the three terms are independent). The interval is M exp(+- z s_lnM) with z = the statistics kernel's sigmaOfLevel(level), default level levelOfSigma(1). The result reports the three terms, the statistical part (dispersion and radius) and the factor's part separately, and the interval with and without the factor's term. The interval does not cover a breakdown of the virial theorem's assumptions (equilibrium, isotropy, a member sample unbiased in radius and velocity); only K's stated uncertainty stands for that, and leg R7 prices a mismodelled factor.
analysisRule.R12: Light. For each member with apparent magnitude m, optional magnitude error, optional K-correction k and extinction A (both in magnitudes, per galaxy, caller's): M_abs = m - DM(z_c) - k - A, DM the cosmology kernel's distance modulus at the cluster redshift; L/L_sun = 10^(-0.4 (M_abs - M_sun)) with M_sun the caller's solar absolute magnitude in that band with its source (no default, empty source refused). The cluster's light is the sum over members brighter than the caller's limiting apparent magnitude; light below the limit is not estimated: the sum is a lower bound unless the caller supplies {fraction, sigma, source} for the missing share, in which case L_total = L_sum / (1 - fraction) with the share's uncertainty carried. Photometric errors propagate in quadrature, sigma_L,i = 0.4 ln10 L_i sigma_m,i, as independent. The mass-to-light ratio is (M / SOLAR_MASS_KG) / (L / L_sun) with the relative uncertainties of the mass interval's own s_lnM and of the light added in quadrature; without the faint-end share it is labelled an upper bound.
analysisRule.R13: Morphology and density. Local projected density of a member is Sigma_N = N / (pi d_N^2) with d_N the projected distance to its N-th nearest other member in the table the caller gives (N the caller's neighbours, no default; a member with fewer than N other members has no density). Neighbours beyond the aperture are not in the table, so the density near the edge is underestimated; the kernel says so. A bin is [lo, hi) in log10 Sigma (the caller's edges); the fraction of a class (the caller's set of labels) is k / n per bin with the exact Clopper-Pearson interval at the stated level (default levelOfSigma(1)); n = 0 returns no fraction. Class labels are data the caller supplies with their source; the kernel holds no classification rule.
analysisRule.R14: Baryon budget. A gas mass is a number the caller cites, {value, sigma, source, aperture}; the kernel forms f_gas = M_gas / M_vir and the baryon fraction (M_gas + M_star) / M_vir with M_star the caller's cited stellar mass, relative uncertainties in quadrature, independent; a gas figure with no source or a non-positive uncertainty is refused, and the kernel states that it is a ratio of two numbers measured in apertures the caller must have matched. No X-ray modelling.
analysisRule.R15: Provenance and labels: every output carries the label of its inputs; a synthetic world is labelled SYNTHETIC with its truth manifest and an authentic table is never accepted without a source field.

worlds.cosmology: flat Lambda-CDM with H0 = 70 km/s/Mpc, Om = 0.3, OL = 0.7: the validation cosmology, round numbers, no radiation, a claim about nothing
worlds.toyCluster: SYNTHETIC. Truncated r^-2 sphere of truncation radius r_t with isotropic Gaussian velocities of one-dimensional dispersion sigma at every radius: a toy, not a dynamically self-consistent system (no equilibrium is asserted); the declared truth is the mass of the singular isothermal halo that would bind such tracers, M(<r_t) = 2 sigma^2 r_t / G. Positions: r = r_t U, cos(theta) uniform in [-1, 1] (so the projected radius is R = r sin(theta)), azimuth uniform; projected onto the sky at (ra0, dec0) by the inverse of the great-circle distance at D_A(z_c). Velocities: v = sigma times a standard normal; z = z_c + (1 + z_c) v / c (the exact inverse of R2). The projected half-number radius is x_half r_t with P(x) = 1 - sqrt(1 - x^2) + x arccos(x) and P(x_half) = 1/2; the factor that makes K sigma^2 R_half / G equal the truth is K_phys = 2 / x_half.
worlds.ensemble: per world index i of a leg's seed: members N log-uniform in [40, 300] (rounded); sigma log-uniform in [400, 1200] km/s; z_c uniform in [0.02, 0.15]; r_t log-uniform in [1, 2] Mpc; ra0 uniform in [0, 360) deg and dec0 uniform in [-60, 60] deg; per-galaxy velocity error 50 km/s declared to the kernel as zErr; interlopers: round(0.02 N) galaxies with velocities uniform in +-8000 km/s about z_c and positions uniform in the aperture disk (the disk of radius 1.001 r_t, which is the aperture given to the kernel); the caller's redshift guess is z_c plus (1 + z_c) u / c with u uniform in +-1500 km/s; no luminosity or class labels except where a leg says
worlds.heavyContamination: the ensemble with round(0.5 N) interlopers (leg D3, R4)
worlds.bimodal: SYNTHETIC. Two equal subclusters, each of velocity dispersion sigma_sub = 400 km/s and N/2 members, centred at +-3 sigma_sub about z_c (a separation of 6 sigma_sub, 2400 km/s), positions as the toy cluster's (r_t = 1.5 Mpc), 2 percent interlopers as in the ensemble; the declared truth is that the sample is not one Gaussian
worlds.light: per world: member absolute magnitudes uniform in [-23, -17] in an invented band, solar absolute magnitude 4.5 (invented, declared to the kernel with source 'invented for the test'), per-galaxy K-correction 0.05 mag and extinction 0.10 mag declared, photometric error 0.05 mag, apparent magnitudes m = M + DM(z_c) + k + A + Gaussian error; the limiting magnitude is M = -19 at the cluster's distance (m_lim = -19 + DM + k + A); truth = the sum of 10^(-0.4 (M_i - M_sun)) over the members with m_i <= m_lim, evaluated on the noise-free apparent magnitudes (the truth set); the kernel selects on the noisy ones, so the edge galaxies are a stated source of disagreement priced in leg C4

x*(kappa), the root of x^2 = V(kappa x), satisfies the residual |x*^2 - V(kappa x*)| <= 1e-12 for kappa in {2, 3, 4, 5}, V written in the leg from the tree's normal density and distribution; x*(3) lies in [0.98, 0.99]; x* increases with kappa (x*(2) < x*(3) < x*(4) < x*(5) < 1); kappa = 1.5 and kappa = sqrt(3) are refused with code 'bad-clip-level'

the plain dispersion of the seven velocities -450, -250, -100, 0, 120, 280, 400 km/s (mean 0, built as redshifts at z_c = 0.0231) equals sqrt(527800/6) km/s to a relative 1e-12 with the truncation correction off, and equals that divided by x*(3) with it on; shifting every redshift by a constant, or permuting them, changes the result by no more than 1e-12 relative; scaling every velocity by 3 scales it by 3 to 1e-12

with a constant per-galaxy velocity error e = 100 km/s (as zErr) the same seven velocities give sigma_int = sqrt(527800/6 - 100^2) with the correction off, and the error of sigma_int is (s / sigma_int) times the plain error s / sqrt(2 (7 - 1)); e = 300 km/s (above s = 296.6) is 'not-constrained' with code 'errors-exceed-scatter'; the biweight option with zErr is refused with code 'errors-with-biweight'

M = K sigma^2 R / G written in the leg from the tree's G_SI and PARSEC_M for (K, sigma km/s, R Mpc) in {(6, 1000, 1), (5.5, 700, 1.5), (10, 400, 0.8)} to a relative 1e-12; s_lnM equals sqrt((sigma_K/K)^2 + (2 sigma_s/sigma)^2 + (sigma_R/R)^2) for sigma_K/K = 0.1, sigma_s/sigma = 0.05, sigma_R/R = 0.08 to 1e-12; the one-sigma interval is M exp(-+ s_lnM); the interval without the factor's term is the same with sigma_K = 0; doubling sigma quadruples M to 1e-12

the kernel refuses or says not-constrained, with the stated code and no number, for: no projection factor ('missing-factor'); a factor with value 0 or negative sigma ('bad-factor'); a factor with an empty source ('missing-factor-source'); a radiusKind that does not match the chosen radius ('factor-radius-mismatch'); a non-flat cosmology and a negative H0 ('refused', 'bad-cosmology'); a galaxy list with a non-finite or non-positive redshift (that galaxy is dropped and counted, never used; a list of only such is 'too-few-members'); an aperture radius of 0 or negative ('bad-aperture'); an empty list ('too-few-members'); a missing solar magnitude or source ('missing-solar-source'); neighbours not a positive integer ('bad-neighbours'); a biweight call without tuning or source ('missing-tuning'); a clip level of 1.5 ('bad-clip-level')

the clip of R4 on a heavily contaminated world with maxPasses forced to 1 returns 'not-constrained' with code 'clip-not-converged' and reports the passes taken; across the 400 worlds of leg C1 the largest pass count is at most 10 and none is not-converged

verdictFunction.what: the kernel verdict, a function of the rows alone: A when every closed-form leg (A1 to A14), every oracle leg (B1 to B5), every refusal core leg (D1, D4, D5), every flag leg (D2, D3) and every coverage leg (C1, C1b, C2, C3, C4, C5) passes; B when the closed-form, oracle and refusal-core legs pass but a coverage or flag leg fails: the closed forms, the dispersion's arithmetic and the mass's arithmetic are claimable and the interval's coverage or the diagnostics are not; C when any closed-form, oracle or refusal-core leg fails: nothing of the kernel is claimable. The product verdict is NOT ESTABLISHED while E1 to E4 are NOT RUN. The consumers clause (a cluster panel, a lesson, a pack, the Coma re-sourcing) is unmet whatever the kernel verdict: Carl's 2026-11-05 consumers rule holds them until a gate passes and no cluster table was supplied.

amendments.what: The oracle is not asked to reproduce the kernel's bootstrap. The kernel's radius uncertainty (a seeded bootstrap on the statistics kernel's stream) is written into the oracle's inputs as a declared number, so the oracle's mass interval is its own three-term algebra (its own analytic dispersion error, the declared radius error, the declared factor error, z from scipy's normal quantile) applied to its own dispersion, radius and distance. The radius and dispersion estimates, the distance and the mass are compared as written; the bootstrap itself is judged only by the coverage legs C1b, C2 and C3.
amendments.why: Recorded before any oracle or validator run, while writing the oracle's inputs: a numpy generator cannot reproduce the tree's mulberry32 stream and a second bootstrap implementation would check nothing about the kernel's.
amendments.when: before any validator run and before any oracle run

amendments.what: The shift invariance of the plain dispersion is tested on the velocities (adding a constant to every velocity changes the dispersion by no more than 1e-12 relative), not on the redshifts: the factor 1 / (1 + z_c) of rule R2 makes a redshift shift change the velocities' scale by a relative delta z / (1 + z_c), which is the rule, not a defect.
amendments.why: Found while reading the committed text against rule R2 before the validator existed: shifting every redshift by a constant also shifts z_c, so the sentence as written would have demanded an invariance R2 forbids. Permutation invariance and the factor-3 scaling are unchanged.
amendments.when: before any validator run and before any oracle run
